title: Contact Form Friction Checklist for Small Businesses

cover.alt: Conceptual contact form with a clear route through a few inputs to a confirmed message.

figures.title: Make each stage easier to complete
figures.summary: The useful comparison is between the visitor’s obstacle and the interface change that removes it.

items.label: Information requested
items.detail: A long set of required details → only the information needed to begin a reply.

items.label: Typing on a phone
items.detail: A generic keyboard for every field → input types suited to email, phone, or URL.

items.label: Next action
items.detail: An ambiguous button → a clear label that explains what will happen.

items.label: After sending
items.detail: A silently cleared form → a visible confirmation of the outcome.

figures.caption: A qualitative map of the friction described in this article, without charting its audit percentages.

figures.title: The form’s job is to start a conversation
figures.summary: Keep the path visible from the first input to the final acknowledgement.

items.label: Identify
items.detail: Give the responder a name and a usable contact method.

items.label: Explain
items.detail: Provide the message or service need.

items.label: Confirm
items.detail: Show the visitor what happened and what to expect next.

figures.caption: A simplified visitor journey derived from the form checklist.
